name: Proxmark3 RDV4 Kit
one_line: Proxmark3 RDV4 RFID/NFC read-write-clone tool sold bundled with HF/LF antennas and case.
why_notable: Same base device as the already-tracked Proxmark3 RDV4.01, sold here as a kit.

name: LAN Tap Pro
one_line: Passive, unpowered Ethernet tap (10/100BASE-T) with two receive-only monitor ports for tapping a wired link.
why_notable: SKU (GSG-LTP) and product description explicitly reference the Throwing Star LAN Tap; same device sold under a different name.

name: YARD Stick One Bundle
one_line: CC1111-based sub-GHz transceiver (YARD Stick One) sold as a bundle.
why_notable: Same base device as the already-tracked YARD Stick One.

name: PortaPack H4M for HackRF
one_line: PortaPack H4M touchscreen/battery display module for HackRF One, sold standalone without a HackRF.
why_notable: Same PortaPack H4M hardware as the already-tracked HackRF + PortaPack H4M combo, sold as the module alone.

name: HackRF + Portapack H4M Combo
one_line: HackRF One SDR transceiver bundled with a PortaPack H4M touchscreen display module.
why_notable: Matches the already-tracked HackRF + PortaPack H4M combo.

name: LAN Tap Kit
one_line: Unassembled solder-it-yourself kit version of the Throwing Star LAN Tap passive Ethernet tap.
why_notable: Description explicitly states it is the DIY kit form of the Throwing Star LAN Tap already tracked.

name: Facedancer21
one_line: USB device emulator/fuzzer board that lets USB device-side protocols be written and driven from host Python code.
why_notable: Same Facedancer project already tracked (generic name), sold here as the specific Facedancer21 hardware revision.

name: CatSniffer
one_line: Multiprotocol IoT sniffer/dev board (TI CC1352, Semtech SX1262, SAMD21) covering sub-GHz, LoRa, BLE and 802.15.4.
why_notable: Description and chipset match the already-tracked CatSniffer V3; this listing just omits the version number.

name: Bus Pirate v5 Kit
one_line: UART/I2C/SPI/1-Wire universal hardware-hacking probe, sold as a kit.
why_notable: Same Bus Pirate 5 hardware already tracked, sold in kit form.

name: WiFi Pineapple Mark VII
one_line: Rogue-AP / man-in-the-middle WiFi auditing platform with the Hak5 PineAP suite and web management UI.
why_notable: Same Hak5 Mark VII hardware as the already-tracked 'WiFi Pineapple Mark VII + AC'; this listing drops the '+AC' bundle suffix.

name: BTLE Sniffer (nRF52840) USB
one_line: nRF52840 USB dongle preloaded with Nordic's BLE sniffer firmware for packet capture in Wireshark/Kismet; re-flashable.
why_notable: Same nRF52840 USB dongle hardware as the already-tracked Nordic nRF52840 Dongle, sold pre-flashed for sniffing.

name: Flux Capacitor for Flipper Zero
one_line: 5V-powered amplified CC1101 sub-GHz module (E07-433M20S, up to 100mW, 425-450MHz) for Flipper Zero.
why_notable: Brand and description match the already-tracked Rabbit-Labs Flux Capacitor (Amplified CC1101).

name: Marauder Pro 2 in 1
one_line: Standalone or Flipper-companion device with ESP32-S2, a 433MHz RF module, GPS module and 2.8in touchscreen, running Marauder firmware.
why_notable: Component set (ESP32-S2 + display + GPS + 433MHz) matches the already-tracked unbranded 'Predator' Module description.
dupe_of: Flipper Zero "Predator" Module (unbranded ESP32-S2 + display + GPS + 433 MHz)

name: YARD Stick One /w Antenna
one_line: CC1111-based sub-GHz transceiver (YARD Stick One) bundled with an antenna.
why_notable: Same base device as the already-tracked YARD Stick One.

name: nRF24 5v Board for Flipper Zero
one_line: 5V nRF24 expansion board with onboard antenna for Flipper Zero, used for 2.4GHz/mousejack work.
why_notable: Same 2.4GHz nRF24 mousejack capability as the already-tracked generic nRF24L01+ Flipper module, this one branded Rabbit-Labs.
dupe_of: nRF24L01+ module for Flipper Zero (mousejack / 2.4 GHz)

name: O.MG Cable Elite
one_line: USB cable with a hidden keystroke/mouse-injection implant, WiFi C2, geofencing triggers, and self-destruct. EUR/GBP not applicable, price range $200-$240 by connector type.
why_notable: Gen-3 'Elite' tier of the already-tracked O.MG Cable product line.

name: NFC Kill Professional
one_line: Handheld ~1600V pulse device for permanently disabling RFID/NFC tags and fuzz-testing RFID readers across 125kHz/13.56MHz/UHF.
why_notable: Same NFC Kill product line already tracked as v3; 'Professional' is a tier/branding variant.

name: MagSpoof v5
one_line: Device that generates an electromagnetic field to spoof/emulate a magnetic-stripe card swipe on standard card readers.
why_notable: Newer hardware revision of the already-tracked MagSpoof project; this listing also claims added read capability and restricts sale to security/LE buyers.

name: T-Dongle S3
one_line: ESP32-S3 board in a USB-dongle form factor with a small display, usable as a BadUSB/USB-Army-Knife platform.
why_notable: Same hardware as the already-tracked LilyGo T-Dongle-S3 (USB Army Knife), listed here without the LilyGo/USB-Army-Knife naming.

name: Chipwhisperer-Lite Bundle
one_line: Side-channel power-analysis and voltage-glitching platform, sold as a bundle.
why_notable: Same ChipWhisperer-Lite (CW1173) hardware already tracked.

name: KeyGrabber
one_line: Inline hardware keylogger (PS/2, USB, or WiFi-exfiltrating variants) that records keystrokes transparently with no drivers or software needed.
why_notable: Long-running hardware keylogger product line, distinct from the AirDrive keylogger already tracked; includes a WiFi-exfiltration variant. Price shown is the low end of a $55-$120 range across models.

name: RTL-SDR
one_line: Generic RTL2832U/R820T USB TV-tuner dongle repurposed as a wideband (24-1850MHz) software-defined radio receiver for GNU Radio/SDR#.
why_notable: Entry-level SDR receiver distinct from the RTL-SDR Blog V4 already tracked (no TCXO/bias-tee/branding).

name: Opera Cake for HackRF
one_line: Antenna-switching add-on for HackRF One with two banks of four RF ports, switchable by frequency or time via command-line control (1MHz-4GHz).
why_notable: Adds automated multi-antenna switching to HackRF, a capability not represented among the existing HackRF entries.

name: WiFi ESP32 Marauder for Flipper Zero
one_line: ESP32-S3 WiFi/Bluetooth analysis add-on for Flipper Zero running Marauder firmware for frame capture, device enumeration, and frame transmission.
why_notable: Third-party ESP32-S3 Marauder devboard for Flipper Zero; a different chip generation from the official ESP32-S2 Wi-Fi Dev Board already tracked.

name: ESP32-MDK for Portapack H4M
one_line: ESP32 add-on module that adds WiFi application support to a HackRF/PortaPack H4M setup.
why_notable: Adds a WiFi radio to the PortaPack/HackRF platform, a capability not present in the existing HackRF entries.

name: iCS Decoder for iCopy-X
one_line: Hardware decoder accessory for the iCopy-X that decodes and clones iCLASS SE/SEO-S cards configured to accept legacy encoding.
why_notable: Extends the already-tracked iCopy-XS to a new high-security card type; a distinct capability-adding accessory, not a passive part.

name: CAN bus for Flipper Zero
one_line: MCP2515-based CAN bus add-on for Flipper Zero that reads, monitors, and resends/replays messages on a vehicle CAN network.
why_notable: Brings automotive CAN bus analysis to the Flipper Zero platform; the DB's automotive category currently has almost no coverage.

name: Masta-Blasta for Flipper Zero
one_line: High-intensity 12-LED infrared blaster add-on for Flipper Zero that extends IR transmit range/power beyond the built-in emitter.
why_notable: Distinct IR-blaster hardware for Flipper Zero from the Rabbit-Labs 'Slim Shady' already tracked (different maker/board).

name: RPi0 USB-A Addon Board
one_line: Pogo-pin add-on board that gives a Raspberry Pi Zero a full-size USB-A port, used to run Responder or PoisonTap-style attacks.
why_notable: Enables a specific named USB-based network credential-theft technique (PoisonTap/Responder), not represented by any existing Pi Zero entry.

name: Gigabit Ethernet Tap
one_line: USB-powered passive single-port 10/100/1000BASE-T network tap with PoE pass-through, in a small metal case.
why_notable: Only Gigabit-capable Ethernet tap seen on the site; the taps already tracked (Throwing Star, Plunder Bug) are 10/100 only.

name: T-Deck Plus Kit
one_line: ESP32 handheld with keyboard, LoRa radio, GPS module, touchscreen, and 2000mAh battery, running Meshtastic or custom firmware.
why_notable: A LilyGo LoRa/GPS handheld distinct from the LilyGo devices already tracked (T-Dongle, T-Embed, T-LoRa Pager, T-Watch).

name: Dual Band WiFi MT7921AU
one_line: USB WiFi 6 adapter (MT7921AU chipset, mt76 driver) that the listing states supports monitor mode and packet injection on 802.11 a/g/n/ac.
why_notable: A monitor-mode/injection-capable WiFi adapter, a device class not otherwise present in the DB.

name: RFID Detector / Diagnostic Card v2
one_line: Credit-card-sized detector with LEDs that light up to indicate the presence and frequency band (125kHz/13.56MHz/860-960MHz) of a nearby RFID reader.
why_notable: An active RFID-reader-detection tool, a different function from the cloning/emulation tools already tracked.

name: Keylogger USB Extension Cable
one_line: Hardware keylogger built into a USB extension cable body, with 16MB flash storage and timestamping, that records USB keyboard input.
why_notable: Same keylogger category as the AirDrive Forensic Keylogger already tracked, but in extension-cable form factor from a different vendor.

name: NExT 13.56MHz and 125kHz Implant
one_line: Injectable glass-capsule RFID/NFC transponder combining an NTAG216 13.56MHz chip and a T5577 125kHz emulator chip for access-control testing.
why_notable: The brief explicitly lists implants as in-scope; the DB currently has no implantable RFID/NFC transponder devices.

name: PortaPack H4M Pro for HackRF Pro
one_line: Touchscreen/battery display module electrically matched to the HackRF Pro (not compatible with HackRF One), running Mayhem firmware.
why_notable: Distinct hardware variant paired specifically with HackRF Pro, not the same PortaPack module used with HackRF One in the tracked combos.

name: WiebeTech Forensic ComboDock v5
one_line: Dual-mode forensic drive dock that forces an explicit choice of write-blocked or read/write mode on power-up to prevent accidental writes to evidence drives.
why_notable: A forensic hardware write-blocker; the brief lists write blockers as in-scope forensics gear and the DB has no existing entries for one.

name: WiebeTech Drive eRazer
one_line: Stand-alone hardware drive wiper that erases SATA/IDE drives at native interface speed without needing a computer.
why_notable: A forensic drive-wiping appliance, filling out the forensics category alongside the ComboDock write-blocker above.

name: 10/100 FastE Switch Tap
one_line: USB-powered 5-port 10/100 Ethernet switch with port mirroring (port 1 to port 5) and PoE pass-through, used as a network tap.
why_notable: A switch-based network tap, mechanically distinct from the passive inline taps already tracked.

name: CANtact v1.2
one_line: Open-source CAN-bus-to-USB interface (fork of the original CANtact) with USB-C and an RJ45-to-OBDII adapter for vehicle and industrial CAN networks.
why_notable: A second automotive CAN interface (alongside the Flipper CAN bus add-on above); a category with almost no existing DB coverage.

name: Multifunction Network Box
one_line: Linux-based network appliance with an LCD status display that logs and selectively blocks traffic across up to 16 GbE ports during an engagement. Price range $1,500-$3,000 by model (Model 100 / Model 1000).
why_notable: A purpose-built covert network-implant/traffic-control box, more capable than the passive taps already tracked, with no equivalent in the DB.

name: BRUSCHETTA Board
one_line: Multi-protocol UART/JTAG/I2C/SPI debugger and programmer supporting 1.8-5V target voltages.
why_notable: An all-in-one hardware-hacking debug probe from a known offensive-security researcher, comparable in role to Bus Pirate/Tigard but not yet tracked.

name: Bluetooth + Battery Module for Proxmark3 RDV4
one_line: Add-on module that gives the Proxmark3 RDV4 Bluetooth connectivity and a battery for untethered, wireless RFID operations.
why_notable: Enables wireless/covert use of the already-tracked Proxmark3 RDV4, but it is an add-on module rather than a standalone device.

name: Rainbow Tables HDD
one_line: 2TB USB 3.0 hard drive preloaded with precomputed rainbow tables for A5/1, WPA-PSK, and MD5 password/hash cracking.
why_notable: It is a generic USB hard drive; its only differentiator is preloaded cracking data, not device hardware capability.

name: Mouse Jiggler
one_line: USB device that enumerates as a mouse and injects small, periodic cursor movements to prevent screen lock and away/idle status.
why_notable: Not an attack tool itself; a covert USB HID device commonly used operationally during physical or remote engagements to prevent session lockout.

name: TP-LINK TL-MR3020 Mini Wireless Router
one_line: Small travel router (802.11n, 150Mbps) explicitly marketed by the listing as OpenWRT and MiniPwner compatible.
why_notable: It's a retail travel router (normally out of scope), but this SKU is sold specifically for reflashing into a MiniPwner-style covert network drop-box.

name: YubiKey NEO
one_line: USB/NFC hardware authentication token supporting OTP, U2F/FIDO, and PIV/OpenPGP smart-card functions.
why_notable: Its purpose is authentication, not offensive or defensive security testing, though it is commonly stocked to demonstrate/test phishing-resistant auth.

name: LockedUSB Charge Only Adapter
one_line: USB adapter that physically disconnects the data lines so a connected device can only charge, blocking juice-jacking attacks.
why_notable: A defensive anti-juice-jacking data blocker rather than an attack tool, but it directly demonstrates/mitigates the O.MG-Cable-style USB data-line attack surface.

name: RFID HF Extender Pro
one_line: Two coupled HF antennas linked by an IPEX cable that relay a 13.56MHz/NFC field between a reader and a remote tag to extend read range.
why_notable: Borders on the 'generic antenna' exclusion, but it specifically enables RFID relay-style range extension between a card and a reader.

name: RFID HF Repeater Large
one_line: 13.56MHz field repeater placed between an obstruction and a reader to amplify coupling and gain a few extra millimeters of tag read distance.
why_notable: Same RFID field-manipulation category as the Extender Pro above, different form factor and use case.

name: RFID HF Field Generator
one_line: Coin-cell-powered 13.56MHz field generator used to power passive HF RFID/NFC tags and implants without a reader present.
why_notable: Borderline because its documented use is powering RFID implants/tags rather than directly attacking a target system.
